speaker: rolf
text: Rolf Ledger. Accountant. I’ve reviewed your finances. You have forty-one dollars, a soup jar and a lanyard that says Vice President. I can help.

choices.label: Make him Treasurer.
choices.hint: Resources · A new ally with ideas
choices.reaction: Rolf opens a laptop. It already has a spreadsheet called {Movement}.

choices.label: We’re not about money.
choices.reaction: Rolf joins anyway. He sits at the back, quietly calculating the value of the folding chairs.

speaker: rolf
text: Membership dues. Five dollars a month. Members who pay feel invested. Members who don’t, leave, which is also a kind of investment.

choices.label: Five dollars a month.
choices.reaction: Forty people pay. Eleven leave. Rolf calls this “a healthy correction”.

choices.label: Free forever.
choices.reaction: Priya hugs you. Rolf makes a note in a spreadsheet tab labelled REGRETS.

speaker: rolf
text: Mugs. {beliefNoun} mugs. Twelve dollars each. I’ve already ordered two hundred, as a hypothetical.

choices.label: Sell the mugs.
choices.reaction: The mugs sell out in a weekend. Agnes refuses to drink from one on principle, then quietly buys two.

choices.label: Return the mugs.
choices.reaction: Rolf returns the mugs. He keeps one, to look at sadly.

speaker: rolf
text: The mugs sold out. Next steps: a {beliefNoun} subscription box, a podcast, and two dollars at the door of every {meeting}.

choices.label: Do all three.
choices.reaction: The podcast is mostly Rolf reading the accounts aloud. It has a loyal audience.

choices.label: Just the podcast.
choices.reaction: Episode one is called “Soup, Margins and You”.

speaker: rolf
text: A soup company wants to sponsor {belief}. Their logo would appear on the {item}. Very small. Medium. It would be medium.

choices.label: Accept the sponsorship.
choices.reaction: The logo is medium-large. Nobody can agree whether it counts as part of the {item} now.

choices.label: Some things aren’t for sale.
choices.reaction: The members cheer. Rolf does not.

speaker: rolf
text: I’ve been patient. This organisation could be a business, and a good one. Either we professionalise, or I take my spreadsheets elsewhere.

choices.label: Professionalise.
choices.reaction: Rolf becomes Chief Financial Officer. He orders business cards for everyone, including Gary, whose says VICE PRESIDENT (DEPUTY).

effects.memory: {Movement} professionalised. Rolf Ledger became Chief Financial Officer.

choices.label: Then take them elsewhere.
choices.reaction: Rolf leaves with three laptops and the good stapler. He says you will hear from him.

speaker: agenda:expansion
text: There’s real interest in {city}. Give me two volunteers and a car, and I’ll have a chapter there by {day}.

choices.label: Go to {city}.
choices.reaction: {speaker} leaves at dawn with two volunteers, a car and a megaphone that may or may not be charged.

choices.label: Focus on {hometown} first.
choices.reaction: {speaker} sighs, then knocks on every door on one street instead.

speaker: agenda:joy
text: {city} has a street festival next month. I could run a stall. Possibly a large stall. Definitely with {beliefNoun}.

choices.label: Run the stall.
choices.reaction: The stall is a hit. Somebody from the council asks for the recipe, and then for a leaflet.

choices.label: Skip the festival.
choices.reaction: The festival happens without you. It is, by all accounts, fine.

speaker: dez
text: Small request. I’d like a title. Director of Recruitment. It would really help with recruiting. People respect directors.

choices.label: Director of Recruitment it is.
choices.reaction: Dez’s business cards arrive the next morning. He had ordered them before asking.

choices.label: No titles.
choices.reaction: Dez puts the business cards back in the box he had ordered them in.

speaker: agnes
text: {title}, your Director of Recruitment has a proposal. Unfortunately, I believe it violates the principles you established last {day}. Dez wants to hold recruitment events during the {day} {meeting}. The {day} {meeting} is for members. It says so in the minutes.

choices.label: Side with Dez. Growth matters.
choices.reaction: Dez sets up a welcome table at the door. Agnes sets up a second table, for minuting the first table.

choices.label: Side with Agnes. Principles matter.
choices.reaction: The {day} {meeting} remains for members. Dez recruits on the pavement outside, which the minutes do not cover.

text: I’m writing a piece on {movement}. Readers want to know: is it true that members spend their evenings {belief}? And who exactly is {title}?

choices.label: Give a full interview.
choices.reaction: The headline reads “Local Group Insists It Is Not a Book Club”. Membership enquiries triple.

choices.label: “No comment.”
choices.reaction: The headline reads “Mysterious Group Declines to Comment”. Membership enquiries double.

speaker: martin
text: The soup situation needs governance. Who decides the soup? Who stirs? I propose a Soup Committee: four members, two-year terms and a stirring rota.

choices.label: Establish the Soup Committee.
choices.hint: Order · Priya loses control of her soup
choices.reaction: The first committee meeting lasts three hours. No soup is made.

choices.label: Priya decides the soup.
choices.reaction: Priya decides on minestrone. It is the correct decision.

speaker: gary
text: The blanket corner is full. I’d like a proper nap room. With a sign. The sign would say NAP ROOM.

choices.label: Build the nap room.
choices.reaction: The NAP ROOM sign is hand-lettered by Gary. The room is never empty.

choices.label: No nap room.
choices.reaction: Gary naps in the car instead. Several members join him. It is a big car.

speaker: agenda:purity
text: Members now refuse to do anything else on {day}s. One missed her own birthday. I propose we make {day} sacred. Officially.

choices.label: {day} is sacred.
choices.reaction: Calendars are amended. Several employers receive identical letters.

choices.label: It’s just a day.
choices.reaction: It is, everyone agrees, just a day. Several people take it personally anyway.

text: Respectfully: some of us work on {day}s. Could {meetings} also happen at weekends? There’s a petition. It has stickers.

choices.label: Add weekend {meetings}.
choices.reaction: Weekend {meetings} are popular, loud and attended by people Agnes describes as “the weekend element”.

choices.label: {day} or nothing.
choices.reaction: The petition is returned, stickers intact.

speaker: agnes
text: I have compiled every decision we have ever made into a rulebook. It is two hundred and twelve pages. Page ninety contradicts page four. I have flagged it.

choices.label: Adopt the rulebook.
choices.reaction: The rulebook is placed on a small table of its own. Nobody is allowed to put a mug on it.

choices.label: Thank you, Agnes. Shelve it.
choices.reaction: The rulebook goes on a shelf. Agnes adds “shelved” to the minutes, with the date.

speaker: agnes
text: I have begun keeping separate minutes. About you. Purely for the historical record. You have said three things this month that contradict the founding statement.

choices.label: Let’s go through them together.
choices.reaction: It takes four hours. Two of the contradictions are resolved. The third becomes a footnote.

choices.label: Stop taking minutes about me.
choices.reaction: Agnes closes the notebook. She opens a different notebook.

speaker: agnes
text: A number of members feel {movement} has drifted from its founding principles. We will be meeting separately, on {day}s, as originally intended. You are welcome to attend. As a guest.

choices.label: Reconcile. Restore the old ways.
choices.reaction: Agnes accepts, on the condition that the reconciliation is minuted. It is.

choices.label: Then go.
choices.reaction: Agnes leaves with forty members and the original minutes. The original minutes were the only copy.

effects.memory: Agnes Thimble founded the Original {movement}, meeting on {day}s, as originally intended.

speaker: martin
text: Dez and I aren’t speaking. He says I’m “killing the vibe with paperwork”. I say paperwork is the vibe. You need to decide who’s right.

choices.label: Martin is right.
choices.reaction: Martin produces a form for formally resolving the dispute. Dez signs it with a very large signature.

choices.label: Dez is right.
choices.reaction: Dez celebrates with the megaphone. Martin files the noise complaint himself.

speaker: priya
text: I made soup for a hundred and forty people this week. My hands smell of onions in my dreams. I need help, or I need to stop.

choices.label: Recruit a soup team.
choices.reaction: The soup team has nine members, matching aprons and, inevitably, a rota.

choices.label: “You’re doing amazing.”
choices.reaction: Priya smiles the smile of someone chopping her nine hundredth onion.

speaker: priya
text: I’m stepping back. From soup, and from most things. I’ll still come on {day}s. I just won’t bring anything.

choices.label: Beg her to stay.
choices.reaction: Priya stays, on the condition that someone else does the onions. Martin volunteers, which surprises everyone.

choices.label: Thank her, and let her rest.
choices.reaction: Priya’s last soup is a quiet minestrone. Several people cry. Gary cries twice.

effects.memory: Priya Moss stepped back. The soup was never quite the same.

text: Someone wore their {item} inside out to the {meeting}. Half the room thinks it’s disrespectful. The other half has started doing it too.

choices.label: Inside out is forbidden.
choices.reaction: A diagram of the correct orientation is pinned to the door.

choices.label: Either way round is fine.
choices.reaction: Within a month, wearing {item} inside out has become a quiet statement of something nobody can define.

text: The Knitting Circle has used this hall for thirty-one years. Your people keep taking our chairs. We are prepared to escalate.

choices.label: Share the hall graciously.
choices.reaction: Mildred accepts. A Knitting Circle member is later seen at a {meeting}, knitting thoughtfully.

choices.label: Outbook them.
choices.reaction: You book every evening for six months. Mildred is seen buying an unusual quantity of wool.

text: We have knitted a banner. It says what we think of {movement}. It is in the town square. It is quite long.

choices.label: Knit a longer banner.
choices.reaction: The banner war makes the regional news. Wool shops report a record month.

effects.memory: {Movement} and the Thursday Knitting Circle fought the Great Banner War.

choices.label: Apologise with {beliefNoun}.
choices.reaction: Mildred accepts the apology. The banner stays up, but someone adds “(sorry)” in different wool.

speaker: martin
text: We’re too big for {title} to decide everything. I propose a board: you, me, and three elected members. It’s good governance. It is also slightly about me.

choices.label: Create the board.
choices.reaction: The first board meeting approves its own existence, unanimously, and then breaks for soup.

choices.label: I am the board.
choices.reaction: Martin nods, and adds “The Board (one person)” to the organisation chart.

text: A small concern from the parents’ group. Members have started bowing to you in the supermarket and calling you Master {initial}. A child asked if you were a wizard.

choices.label: Tell them to stop bowing.
choices.reaction: The bowing becomes a small, discreet nod. Somehow this is more unsettling.

choices.label: Bowing is fine. I am not a wizard.
choices.reaction: The child is not convinced. Neither, increasingly, is anyone else.

speaker: dez
text: The backward-walking video has two million views. Most of the comments are confused. Some are just a picture of a crab.

choices.label: Backward march through {hometown}.
choices.reaction: Four hundred people walk backward down the high street. Two walk into a bakery. The bakery joins.

choices.label: Stay humble.
choices.reaction: Dez posts a single, humble follow-up video. It is also walking backward.

speaker: gary
text: Proposal: Whale Wednesday. One evening a week where we just talk about whales. I’ve prepared slides. There are ninety slides.

choices.label: Whale Wednesday is official.
choices.reaction: Attendance at Whale Wednesday overtakes the main {meeting} by week three.

choices.label: Once a month.
choices.reaction: Gary accepts. The slides are reorganised into a monthly epic.

text: I’ve been to every {meeting} since the garage. Every single one. I don’t want much. Maybe a pin.

choices.label: Brenda gets a pin.
choices.reaction: Brenda wears the pin everywhere, including in the bath.

choices.label: We don’t do pins.
choices.reaction: Brenda makes her own pin. It is better than any pin you would have made.

speaker: agenda:order
text: Since Brenda got her pin, four hundred people want pins. There is now a Pin Committee, which wants its own pin.

choices.label: Pins for everyone.
choices.reaction: Pins are distributed. A secondary market in rare pins emerges within a fortnight.

choices.label: Pins must be earned.
choices.reaction: The Pin Committee publishes eligibility criteria. They are forty pages long.

anon.name: Kevin Pruitt
anon.role: Member, claims to be a founder

text: I want it on the record that I invented {belief}. I was there. Possibly. It was dark.

choices.label: Thank Kevin publicly.
choices.reaction: Kevin is thanked at the {meeting}. Priya, Gary and three others quietly look at each other.

choices.label: Kevin did not invent it.
choices.reaction: Kevin accepts this with the face of a man who will write a book.

text: My memoir is out. It’s called “I Invented {belief}”. Chapter nine is about you. It is not kind.

choices.label: Buy every copy.
choices.reaction: You buy every copy. Kevin orders a second printing with the proceeds.

choices.label: Ignore it.
choices.reaction: The book sells forty copies, all in {hometown}. Everyone has read chapter nine.

speaker: agenda:order
text: The {city} chapter wants its own leader and its own {meeting} night. They say {hometown} doesn’t understand them.

choices.label: Give {city} its own leader.
choices.reaction: The new {city} leader’s first act is to change the snacks. Nobody in {hometown} is told what to.

choices.label: All decisions come from {hq}.
choices.reaction: {city} accepts. Its minutes become noticeably shorter.

speaker: martin
text: Some members want to do more. I’d like to run an organiser course: how to start a chapter, how to book a hall, how to stop Dez promising lunch.

choices.label: Train organisers.
choices.reaction: The course has twelve graduates. Their final project is a laminated guide to lamination.

choices.label: People can learn on the job.
choices.reaction: They do learn on the job, mostly from Dez, which explains a lot.

speaker: agenda:order
text: Odd thing. The petty cash buys a lot of biscuits. More biscuits than we have members. Someone is eating a great many biscuits.

choices.label: Investigate.
choices.reaction: The investigation finds that Gary has been feeding the biscuits to a family of foxes. The foxes are now considered members.

choices.label: Biscuits are morale.
choices.reaction: The biscuit budget doubles. Nobody asks where they go.

speaker: any
text: We’re in {towns} towns now. People in places I’ve never been are arguing about {belief}. We need a regional structure. Or we need to accept that we don’t control this any more.

choices.label: Build a regional structure.
choices.reaction: Martin unrolls a map of the region. He has already drawn on it, in three colours.

effects.memory: {Movement} became a regional organisation, with a map in three colours.

choices.label: Let it grow wild.
choices.reaction: Dez is delighted. Martin quietly rolls up the map.

effects.memory: {Movement} spread across the region without a plan, which some called a plan.
